notes.decision: The bracketed restoration in the header position does not correspond to the standard Coptic numeral for 193 (= ⲣϥⲅ). It may represent a corrupt or partial reading by the editor, or possibly a Greek loanword (πῦρ 'fire') functioning as a section/chapter title element rather than a numeral. Preserved as transcribed with apparatus note.

Parsed as Lycopolitan infinitive ⲉ-ⲣ̄- + ⲕⲁⲁⲥ ('place/set her,' Sah. ⲕⲱ + 3sgf object). Refers to setting/establishing the mercy (ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ, fem.) — the catechumen establishes the first 'great mercy' in some institutional locus.

Recurring Lycopolitan verbal forms of 'give' (ϯ) with object suffixes: -ⲥ 'her', -ϩ 'him', -ⲧⲟⲩ 'them.' Stem ⲧⲉⲉ- functions as the verbal element. The ⲛ̄ϩ- onset is likely conjunctive/circumstantial prefix. Translated 'giving (X to Y)' throughout for consistency.

Indefinite noun denoting 'something, some help, alms.' The compound parsing is unclear: possibly ⲟⲩ-ⲃⲁ-ⲟⲩⲁⲛ ('a thing of any kind') or related to a Lyc. lexeme for 'aid/relief.' Translated 'some help' from context (paired with redeeming one in affliction and giving to righteousness — almsgiving register).

Translated 'chosen (matter).' The lexeme ⲥⲁⲧⲧ here is parallel to ⲛϩⲱⲃ 'matter' (cf. line 4 ⲡⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲛϩⲱⲃ 'the second matter'). Likely substantival use of ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ ('chosen, elect, choice item,' qualitative of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄) with -ⲧⲧ for -ⲧⲡ̄ orthographic Lyc variation. The catechumen's 'three chosen matters' = his three obligated good works of mercy. Distinct from the proper-noun usage of ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ ('the chosen one' = Zarathustra) in earlier kephalaia.

Parsed as perfect 3pl ⲁⲩ-ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ('they have honored') + direct object ⲙ̄ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ ('the mercies'). The subject 'they' refers either to the elect/community as recipients, or to the mercies themselves being honored. ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ here is the verb 'honor' (cf. ⲧⲁⲓⲟ in glossary), distinct from the homograph ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ 'kind/category.' Confirmed by line 19's ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ 'honor among them' and line 20's ⲟⲩⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲁⲧ 'an honor of grace' — the same kephalaion uses ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ as 'honor.'

Treated as the chapter-numbering marker '81' (Coptic numeral ⲡ̄ⲁ̄ = 80+1). The marker appears at line 23 (alone) and at end of line 25, possibly bracketing the chapter heading. Alternatively, ⲡⲁ could function as the Lycopolitan relative-marker 'the one of / concerning,' but the bracketing arrangement and the new chapter context favor the numerical reading. Translated '(81)' to flag the marker's structural function.

Translated 'Concerning the begetting of a multitude of angels' as the topic-incipit of Kephalaion 81. The opening ⲡⲁ functions as 'the one of / concerning'; ⲥⲭⲡⲟ (Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget') is the action-noun. The trailing ⲡⲁ likely repeats the chapter number as a closing-bracket marker.

Visible 1sg perfect prefix ⲁⲓ- + verb-stem ⲱ-. Possibilities: ⲁⲓⲱ(ⲱ) 'I have conceived,' ⲁⲓⲱⲗ 'I have come,' ⲁⲓⲱⲡ 'I have reckoned/counted,' or ⲁⲓⲱⲱⲡⲉ 'I have become.' Followed by lacuna of ~3 chars. Mani is speaking autobiographically, having just confirmed the doctrine of seven angels begotten of fasting. The lacuna content is irrecoverable; left untranslated.

Translated 'leader.' The form is most likely Greek παρα-ἀρχηγός 'co-leader / one-alongside-the-founder,' or possibly παράγωγος 'leader-aside, conductor, guide.' Mani is identifying himself as the apostolic leader/initiator of his church. The Greek prefix παρα- ('alongside') may emphasize his role as the appointed-by-side companion-figure of the cosmic powers, or as 'the secondary leader' under the Father. Cf. accumulated ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲏⲅⲟⲥ 'the leaders/chiefs' (without the παρα- prefix). The whole sentence asserts Mani's apostolic primacy: 'since I am the leader, while the fifty elect were with me in the church, while I was head over her.'
